messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: ALERT: High eviction rate in us-west-2 serving pool (ephemeral storage pressure). Affected pods: model-serve-* in namespace prod-serve. Symptoms: repeated pod restarts, OOMs logged by runtimes, CUDA init failures after restart. Impact: ~5-15% increased 5xx across live traffic. Paging oncall now.
sophia: I’m on it. grabbing metrics and node list. Can someone post the node disk usage? @ryan can you run a quick du on /var/scratch and /var/log on the suspect nodes?
ryan: looking… found 3 nodes with /var/scratch > 92% and massive modelcache dirs. quick commands:
```
kubectl get pods -n prod-serve -o wide | grep model-serve
ssh node-172-31-42-11 -- df -h /var/scratch
ssh node-172-31-42-11 -- sudo du -sh /var/scratch/modelcache/* | sort -h | tail -n 20
```
ryan: output shows modelcache shards + rotated logs piling up: largest file set is modelcache/llama_v2/chunk-*.bin ~120G each (old versions).
sophia: ok. are kubelet eviction thresholds kicking? any OOMKill events?
james: logs from one pod:
```
[2026-03-15T02:05:12Z] runtime: cuda: failed to init gpu context: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[2026-03-15T02:05:13Z] runtime: process terminated: signal SIGABRT (core dumped)
kubelet: Pod model-serve-7 restarted 4 times due to OOMKill
```
james: also saw container crashloop shortly after large cache write during model reload.
ryan: looks like model cache eviction + concurrent model load triggers big write spikes; journalctl shows heavy writeback causing node to move to DiskPressure -> pod eviction.
sophia: immediate mitigation steps: 1) cordon two most affected nodes. 2) scale down noncritical batch jobs writing to /var/scratch. 3) delete stale modelcache versions for deer-dev models (safe per James). 4) rotate and compress logs. 5) set model-serve pods to use tmpfs for cache for next deploy (if feasible).
alicia: I can take node cordon/drain ops. Doing: `kubectl cordon node-172-31-42-11` then `kubectl drain node-172-31-42-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — will move pods; risk: more cache reloads. recommend streaming canary to other region if we see more 5xx.
ops-bot: deploy-bot queued: manual redeploy of model-serve will pull latest cache config if PR merged.
james: to reduce reload pressure, pushing a quick patch to runtime: avoid simultaneous bulk writes by staggering model downloads (backoff jitter). Patching now and will roll to 10% canary.
ryan: cleaned up ~600GB of old binary shards from node-172-31-42-11 and rotated logs (gzip). freed ~700G. monitoring disk reclaim.
sophia: nice. after cleanup, eviction rate dropped to near zero on that node. kubelet reports healthy. telemetry: 5xx rate down from 12% to 2% over 10 minutes.
alicia: handing off to night oncall (alicia). summary for handoff:
- root cause: unbounded modelcache growth + stale shards + heavy background model reloads caused sustained writeback -> DiskPressure -> pod evictions. Some pods experienced OOM/CUDA errors immediately after restart, likely due to GPU memory fragmentation on restart.
- mitigation performed: cordoned/drained two worst nodes, removed stale shards (~600GB), compressed logs, scaled down batch writers, temporarily pinned critical customers to instances in eu-west-1, applied traffic steering to reduce load on us-west-2. Started a canary runtime rollout to add jittered model downloads.
- impact: transient 5xx spikes (peak ~15% of requests) for 18 minutes, affected customers: two enterprise tenants reported increased latency and intermittent 503s — CS notified.
- follow-ups (assigned):
  - ry an: create retention policy + GC for modelcache shards (PR: infra/modelcache-gc) — blocker: needs migration plan for pinned models.
  - james: add runtime-level backpressure for concurrent model downloads and safer gpu-init retry strategy.
  - sophia: improve alerting for sustained writeback + DiskPressure (thresholds and pager suppression for known maintenance windows).
  - ops: propose ephemeral partition size check in node bootstrap and a preflight job that verifies free space before heavy model loads.
- logs/artifacts: linked artifacts and kube events uploaded to /mnt/incidents/4082468012/ (ops: confirm access).
sophia: tagging @alicia for handoff. alicia — anything you need me to add before I sign off?
alicia: grabbing acceptance. can you paste the cleanup commands you ran so I can document them?
ryan: cleanup commands I used:
```
sudo find /var/scratch/modelcache -maxdepth 2 -name "*.bin" -mtime +30 -print -exec rm -f {} \;
sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=3d
gzip -9 /var/log/model-serve/*.log.2026*
systemctl restart kubelet
```
alicia: copying into postmortem notes. I'll own the follow-ups and open a Sev-C postmortem doc. Taking over pager and will watch metrics for 3 hours. handoff complete.
sophia: thanks team. marking incident as stabilized, moving to monitoring. :white_check_mark:
